advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Consider having the pytester self-test import the real fixture (or assert the inline copy matches conftest) so the fixture wiring cannot silently drift from what ships.
evidence: _GUARDED_CONFTEST fixture body at tests/unit/test_caplog_coverage_integrity.py:119-133 is structurally identical to the real fixture at tests/conftest.py:493-508 (same setup fail, same try/finally restore_level, same teardown fail)

The module docstring states the shared-primitives split exists so the self-test drives 'the *same* logic instead of a copy that could drift' (tests/_log_integrity.py header) — but only the detection PRIMITIVES are shared; the fixture wiring is copied

This mirrors the established convention in tests/unit/test_repo_isolation_guard.py:26 which uses the same inline-conftest-string approach, so the drift risk is a known repo-wide tradeoff, not novel to this change
advisory.finding: The pytester self-test's _GUARDED_CONFTEST inlines a verbatim hand-copy of the real autouse fixture body (setup/teardown propagation checks + level snapshot/restore) rather than importing it, so the self-test can silently validate stale wiring if tests/conftest.py's _rebar_log_propagation_guard later changes (e.g. adds a phase or reorders the checks) without a matching edit to the string.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the pytester self-tests drive the REAL conftest fixture (e.g. import/reuse the actual fixture via a shared helper or `pytester.copy_example`/`makeconftest` sourced from the real file) instead of a verbatim inline copy that can drift from tests/conftest.py.
evidence: `_GUARDED_CONFTEST` (lines 108-134) re-declares `_rebar_log_propagation_guard` inline as a string, and every pytester test installs it via `pytester.makeconftest(_GUARDED_CONFTEST.format(...))` (e.g. lines 167, 182, 209, 228) — the real fixture at tests/conftest.py:492-508 is never the code under test in these end-to-end cases.

The module docstring claims the split 'lets the guard's self-test exercise the *same* logic instead of a copy that could drift' (tests/_log_integrity.py:33-35), but that guarantee covers only the _log_integrity primitives; the fixture wiring in conftest.py is duplicated verbatim in the test file and IS the copy that can drift.

Regression-blindness: an edit to the real conftest fixture (e.g. deleting `_log_integrity.restore_level(baseline_level)` at conftest.py:504) leaves _log_integrity.py unchanged, so all 11 self-tests stay green while the guard's level-containment contract is broken.
advisory.finding: The pytester self-tests exercise a hand-copied duplicate of the autouse fixture (`_GUARDED_CONFTEST`), not the real fixture in tests/conftest.py, so a behavior-affecting change to the real fixture body (e.g. removing the `finally: restore_level(baseline)` containment, dropping the setup-phase `restore_propagation()`, or reordering the setup/teardown checks) would not be caught by any self-test — the copy can drift from the guard it purports to verify.
scenarios: A future refactor edits the real tests/conftest.py fixture body but not _log_integrity.py; the containment or blame behavior regresses and the suite stays green.
advisory.suggested_fix: Extract the fixture body into a reusable factory in tests/_log_integrity.py (or a small importable module) that both tests/conftest.py and the pytester conftest call, so the self-test exercises the same fixture code rather than a hand-maintained duplicate.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a pytester scenario that leaves `rebar` propagation False before a guarded test's setup (out-of-band poisoning) and asserts the guarded run errors at setup with the 'already off when ... started' message and restores propagation for later tests.
evidence: `test_setup_phase_reports_an_out_of_band_poisoning` (lines 64-75) asserts only the primitive's returned message; it does not run the fixture.

The pytester scenarios (`_POISONED_TESTS`, lines 96-106) poison propagation mid-capture, which the fixture catches at the TEARDOWN branch (conftest.py:505-508); none pre-sets propagation False before a guarded test starts to hit the setup branch at conftest.py:496-499.
ABSENCE rationale: the setup-phase failure-and-restore path in the actual fixture has no behavior-level test asserting it fails the run and restores propagation.
advisory.finding: No end-to-end (pytester) test drives the real/guarded fixture's SETUP-phase failure branch — an out-of-band poisoning where `rebar` propagation is already False at test setup, which should make the guard fail at setup and restore propagation. Only the message-producing primitive is unit-tested for phase='setup'; the fixture's setup-phase `pytest.fail` + `restore_propagation()` wiring is never exercised through the fixture.
scenarios: A change that breaks the setup-phase branch (e.g. failing to restore propagation, or mis-classifying setup vs teardown) would not be caught end-to-end.
